gloss: to feel dizzy; to be dazzled; to be blinded

definitions.gloss: to feel dizzy; to have one's head spin
definitions.explanation: To experience a sensation of dizziness or lightheadedness, often from looking down from a height or standing up suddenly.

definitions.gloss: to be dazzled; to be blinded; to lose one's judgment
definitions.explanation: To have one's vision or judgment impaired, either by bright light or figuratively by greed, desire, or temptation.

examples.japanese: {高|たか}い{所|ところ}から{下|した}を{見|み}て{目|め}が{眩|くら}んだ。
examples.english: I looked down from a high place and felt dizzy.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{上|あ}がったら{目|め}が{眩|くら}んだ。
examples.english: I felt dizzy when I stood up.

examples.japanese: {太陽|たいよう}の{光|ひかり}に{目|め}が{眩|くら}んだ。
examples.english: I was blinded by the sunlight.

examples.japanese: {金|かね}に{目|め}が{眩|くら}んで{悪事|あくじ}に{手|て}を{染|そ}めた。
examples.english: Blinded by money, he turned to crime.

examples.japanese: {欲|よく}に{目|め}が{眩|くら}んで{大切|たいせつ}なものを{見失|みうしな}ってはいけない。
examples.english: You must not be blinded by greed and lose sight of what's important.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{立|た}ち{上|あ}がると{目|め}が{眩|くら}むことがあるので{気|き}をつけてください。
examples.english: Please be careful, as standing up suddenly can cause dizziness.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the pattern {目|め}が{眩|くら}む. The figurative sense ({金|かね}に{目|め}が{眩|くら}む — to be blinded by money) is very common.

GRAMMAR:
Godan verb (u-verb). Intransitive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目|め}が{眩|くら}む (to feel dizzy; to be dazzled)
- {金|かね}に{目|め}が{眩|くら}む (to be blinded by money)
- {欲|よく}に{目|め}が{眩|くら}む (to be blinded by greed)
